subQuests.subQuestName: Approach the wooden cabin on the ice

772110102.text: #Do you hear that, {NICKNAME}? That rustling, it sounds like it's coming from inside that wooden house...

772110103.text: Chulkaturin! Hello! Chulkaturin? Are you still in there?

772110105.text: Ah, it is you, shorebound travelers.

772110106.text: So you were inside! Come on out, quickly! The ice is about to melt — your home's gonna sink!

772110107.text: Yes. The ice is melting away.

772110110.text: Ashore... Thank you, travelers by the shore, but...

772110111.text: No, I shall not leave this house.

772110112.text: Are you serious!? This is not the time for that! If you don't get ashore, you're gonna go under!

772110113.text: If this place that I could set my feet upon, this final place that belongs to me, must end in this moment and inexorably sink, then I accept it. This, too, shall be my fate.

772110114.text: It was I who insisted upon increasing its weight. I wished, in my infinitesimal greed, to restore but a shade of our former glory and dignity, to expand my dwelling, and so overburdened that piece of floe...

772110115.text: But this house... No matter the outcome, it is my final resting place. It has borne my flesh, and it carries all my history.

772110116.text: It and I were ever only relics of the olden times. And if I were to step forth from its doors, I would never again find rooting in this world.

772110117.text: What are you talking about!? Do you mean you're just gonna die?

772110118.text: I was always a ghost of history, shorebound travelers. I bear a past I cannot cast aside, indeed, I have borne it long enough.

772110119.text: Anyone can dock by the shore, save for me, traveler, for they have new lives they may live.

772110120.text: But not me. Should I wish to start a new life, I shall have to atone for the past — the all-too-heavy, all-too-stubborn past, which has long become a part of my life, one I cannot cut free.

772110121.text: If silence comes in this moment, then I say, let it come. This is the fate I have awaited all these years.

772110122.text: You still have a chance to choose your destiny...

772110124.text: As long as you know the law the wind follows, even on the river current, you can, in large part, know the path you shall take.

772110125.text: But on land... Though the wind that sweeps through it has never changed paths in these hundreds of years, this land's future can never be predicted.

772110126.text: Should I step on land... should I tread upon soil estranged and step into its unknowable future, how many of my choices would belong to "me" then?

772110127.text: Oh no, more and more of the ice is melting...

772110128.text: C'mon, Chulkaturin, enough of this talk about choices. Come down! We can talk about this stuff later.
